question: A man goes to Lucknow from Kanpur at a speed of 18 km/hr and returns to Kanpur at speed of 36 km/hr, through the same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the same distance is covered at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed is given by the direct formula:

Average speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

⇒ Average speed = (2 × 18 × 36) ÷ (18 + 36)

⇒ Average speed = (2 × 18 × 36) ÷ 54 = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Kanpur to Lucknow (S₁) = 18 km/hr

Speed from Lucknow to Kanpur (S₂) = 36 km/hr

Let the distance between Kanpur and Lucknow be d km.

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance for the entire journey = d + d = 2d

⇒ Time taken to reach Lucknow (T₁) = d ÷ 18 hours

⇒ Time taken to return to Kanpur (T₂) = d ÷ 36 hours

⇒ Total Time = (d ÷ 18) + (d ÷ 36)

⇒ Total Time = (2d + d) ÷ 36 = 3d ÷ 36 = d ÷ 12 hours

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 2d ÷ (d ÷ 12)

⇒ Average Speed = 2d × 12 ÷ d = 24 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 24 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z respectively, the direct formula is: Average Speed = (3xyz) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, relative speed is the difference of their speeds (V₁ − V₂). When moving in opposite directions, it is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂).

General Average Speed Rule

If the distances traveled at different speeds are unequal, strictly use the fundamental formula (Total Distance ÷ Total Time). Never simply calculate the arithmetic mean of the given speeds.
